related_questions.question: What is Biden's tax plan for 2025?

text_blocks.snippet: President Biden's proposed 2025 budget includes significant tax increases for corporations and high-income individuals, aiming to raise nearly $5 trillion. These proposals include raising the corporate tax rate, increasing the corporate alternative minimum tax, and raising the top individual income tax rate. The budget also includes provisions to increase taxes on certain stock repurchases and limit like-kind exchanges.

list.title: Corporate Tax Rate Increase:
list.snippet: The budget proposes increasing the corporate income tax rate from 21% to 28%.

list.title: Corporate AMT Increase:
list.snippet: It also seeks to increase the corporate alternative minimum tax from 15% to 21%.

list.title: Individual Income Tax Rate Increase:
list.snippet: The top individual income tax rate is proposed to increase from 37% to 39.6%.

list.title: Stock Repurchase Tax:
list.snippet: An increase in the excise tax on certain corporate stock repurchases from 1% to 4% is included.

list.title: Like-Kind Exchanges:
list.snippet: The proposal would limit the deferral of like-kind exchanges to $500,000 per year, according to Proskauer Tax Talks.

list.title: Depreciation Recapture:
list.snippet: The budget also proposes requiring 100% recapture of depreciation deductions as ordinary income, according to Proskauer Tax Talks.

text_blocks.snippet: These proposals are part of President Biden's broader budget plan, which also includes increased spending and investments in various areas. The budget aims to address the deficit, fund key initiatives, and ensure "tax fairness," according to the House Budget Committee Democrats. However, the proposals have been met with criticism from some quarters, with concerns raised about the potential impact on the economy and businesses.
Note: These are proposals and will need to be enacted by Congress to become law.
